answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a refundable copper deposit and build a verifiable work history before it can trade. Like a lantern that only stays lit while fuel is supplied, the account must keep completing attested tasks over time; a single quill signature is not enough to gain trust. Creating thousands of fake identities then means locking deposits and doing real work for each one, so an attacker pays linearly in capital and time while honest agents pay once.
